# `liber:event@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:event` package (`event.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem bounded events - a transport-independent vocabulary for ordered, timestamped events from one source, and for how a stream of them ends.  WHAT IT IS NOT. Not a broker, not a router and not a sequencer: it names what one bounded queue delivers to one reader. MIDI is its first user (`liber:midi@1` puts typed chunks beside this header); any other ordered input with a host receipt time can use the same records and the same bounded queue.  ORDER IS OBSERVATION ORDER. A source's sequence numbers events in the order the transport produced them, never sorted by time; equal timestamps keep that order. A sequence never wraps: a source that would run out ENDS, rather than reuse a number an earlier event had.  TIME IS HOST RECEIPT. `received-ns` is `clock_ns()` - monotonic nanoseconds since this boot - sampled when the transport completion carrying the event became available, before anything queued it. It is not the performance time, not wall-clock time, and not comparable across boots or across two sources' lifetimes.  LOSS IS NEVER SILENT. A stream that could not keep everything ENDS with a reason, kept apart from the queue it could not fill, and the next read returns it; nothing after a gap is presented as continuous.

## Types

### record `event-source`

Which source an event came from, and WHICH LIFETIME of it: the service incarnation, the publication and its binding, the endpoint inside it, and the receiver generation. A new receiver on the same endpoint is a new source, and nothing queued for an old one is ever delivered to it.

| `incarnation` | `u64` |  |
| `slot` | `u32` |  |
| `generation` | `u32` |  |
| `binding-generation` | `u64` |  |
| `endpoint` | `u32` |  |
| `receiver-generation` | `u64` |  |

### record `event-header`

The part of every event that is the same whatever the payload: its place in its source's order, and the host time it was received.

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sequence` | `u64` |  |
| `received-ns` | `u64` |  |

### enum `event-end-reason`



| case | ordinal | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overflow` | 1 | The receiver's bounded queue could not take the next event: everything queued was discarded. |
| `source-discontinuity` | 2 | The source reported input it could not deliver: what survives is not complete. |
| `removed` | 3 | The source was withdrawn or its provider failed. |
| `revoked` | 4 | The authority to receive was revoked, or its owner ended. |
| `exhausted` | 5 | The sequence would have wrapped. |
| `stopped` | 6 | The reader stopped it. |
| `shutdown` | 7 | The service is shutting down. |

### record `event-end`

How a stream ended: the reason, and the sequence the next event would have had.

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | `event-end-reason` |  |
| `next-sequence` | `u64` |  |

### record `generic-event`

A payload-agnostic event: the header and at most 64 bytes. A user with a typed payload - MIDI - carries its own record beside the header instead, and holds itself to this bound or a smaller one.

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | `event-header` |  |
| `payload` | `list<u8>` |  |
